feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications roles: the progression at NACo is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target title. Writing is polished overall, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, less repetition across skills sections, and a few consistency edits.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear career progression within one organization, showing increasing responsibility from coordinator to director to consultant.  
- Strong domain credibility: Drupal, analytics stack, governance, multimedia, and advocacy/public-sector communications are all well evidenced.  
- Good clarity and readability in the summary and experience bullets; achievements like the 10,000+ page migration and in-house studio stand out.

1. Top improvements  
- Add more measurable outcomes beyond activity/scope: e.g., email growth, engagement improvements, traffic gains, production efficiencies, cost savings, or adoption results from governance/workflow changes.  
- Reduce duplication between “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT”; consolidate to tighten structure and save space.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “12 years of experience”; choose one style for serial commas (“web, content, email, social media, and multimedia” vs “web, email, social and multimedia”); “A2/Learning” is awkward—use “A2 (learning)” or “Elementary (A2).” No major misspellings found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary with clear positioning for digital communications leadership. It aligns well with the CV, but it’s slightly generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner, more standard phrasing.
- Add one concrete differentiator from recent roles, such as enterprise web modernization, Drupal-led transformation, or analytics/governance leadership.
- Tighten broad phrases like “workflows and systems” by linking them to outcomes: scalable publishing, cross-team coordination, or mission delivery.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading web, email, social media, content, and multimedia programs for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, enterprise web modernization, editorial governance, and digital operations. Strong track record translating policy and technical issues into clear public-facing content, aligning stakeholders, and building scalable systems that improve coordination, publishing, and audience engagement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications” and “stakeholder coordination” duplicate Core Competencies/Soft Skills language.
- “Workflows and systems” overlaps with multiple skills sections; make it more specific here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block is broad and overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. Tightening the phrasing and emphasizing leadership-level capabilities will make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel, higher-value phrasing: “Digital transformation leadership” instead of “Digital strategy & transformation.”
- Replace generic terms with sharper ones: “Cross-channel communications leadership,” “CMS and web operations,” “Content governance and editorial workflows.”
- Group related items to reduce list fatigue and improve scanability; proposed version:
  Digital transformation leadership • Cross-channel communications leadership • CMS and web operations • Content governance and editorial workflows • Analytics, reporting and optimization • Workflow architecture and systems design • Stakeholder and cross-functional alignment • Advocacy and policy communications • Multimedia and live event production
- Standardize style: use either “cross-functional” or “cross-department” consistently across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication,” “stakeholder coordination,” and “policy & advocacy communication” repeat the header and Topline Skills almost verbatim.
- “Web & CMS administration” and “data analytics & reporting” overlap with Technical + IT and Analytics sections.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo entries. Tighten it around what is new in this consulting engagement: advisory scope, technical delivery, and the AI/search initiative.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as 3–4 impact-led bullets, e.g.:
- Advise NACo on enterprise digital strategy, content operations, and platform improvements across web, email, social, and multimedia channels.
- Designed and implemented Drupal-based campaign experiences, including modular microsites, reusable content components, and member-facing resource/toolkit pages.
- Improved communications workflows, analytics, and governance to support more coordinated cross-department publishing and decision-making.
- Leading an AI-enabled site search initiative spanning retrieval strategy, structured content design, and user-facing discovery experience.
- Replace weak verbs like “consult,” “build and refine,” and “deliver” with “advise,” “designed,” “implemented,” “improved,” or “led.”
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages/templates, publishing time reduced, search accuracy/engagement gains, or stakeholder teams supported.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” and broad channel oversight repeat the Director role; keep this version focused on consulting-specific outcomes.
- Avoid restating general CMS/front-end troubleshooting if those skills already appear elsewhere.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals; it should be tightened to emphasize outcomes and distinguish clearly from your earlier NACo role. Right now, some bullets read as scope descriptions rather than achievements.

Suggested edit:
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Add measurable results where possible for email/social/video/analytics: growth %, engagement lifts, production savings, faster reporting, reduced vendor spend, or improved publishing efficiency.
- Tighten phrasing and reduce platform lists: “Built NACo’s first in-house broadcast studio, increasing capacity for advocacy programming, events, and recurring multimedia content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Editorial coordination/workflows” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership, transformation, and infrastructure.
- Video expansion also appears in earlier NACo roles; here, emphasize the studio build and organizational-scale impact.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and the earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about execution, channel growth, and editorial operations at the manager-to-director transition stage.

Suggested edit
- Open with a tighter scope/result line: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media and video, strengthening editorial coordination and advocacy messaging.”
- Combine and sharpen bullets around owned outputs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with stronger ownership where accurate: “Improved digital publishing workflows and cross-team editorial planning across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” is very close to the Director role’s opening; use “managed” or “oversaw execution” here.
- “Weekly advocacy video update” also appears in the 2015–2018 role; distinguish this entry as scaling/operationalizing the format, not launching it.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinctive strengths rather than broad communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, higher-seniority wording: “Enterprise digital strategy” → “Enterprise digital strategy and platform modernization.”
- Make governance and operating-model strength more explicit: “Editorial systems and governance” → “Editorial governance, publishing workflows, and content operations.”
- Narrow “Multi-channel communications leadership” to avoid vagueness: “Cross-channel digital communications leadership.”
- Consider revised version:
- Enterprise digital strategy and platform modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows, and content operations
- Cross-channel digital communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership, and advocacy messaging
- Audience-centered content strategy and planning

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Audience-focused content planning” is already implied by the header and multiple work entries; keep only if you need a softer content-strategy note.
- “Multi-channel communications leadership” duplicates “Multi-channel communication” in Core Competencies almost verbatim.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery

- Workflow automation

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a raw keyword dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills area, emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and group tools under broader strengths.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped, impact-oriented phrases rather than a long list: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages • CMS modernization and front-end implementation • API integrations and workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search and content discovery”
- Prioritize recent strengths tied to current/most recent roles: put Drupal, CMS modernization, front-end implementation, and AI-enabled search first.
- Tighten “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” to “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery)” so it signals application, not just syntax knowledge.
- If space allows, replace one generic item with scale/context: “Enterprise CMS modernization” or “Large-scale Drupal migrations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills broader and leave full tool inventory to the technical section.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with “Automation & Workflow Systems.”

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery

- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster that aligns well with the recent Director/Consultant roles, but it reads as a raw tool list rather than a value-focused capability statement. Tightening the phrasing and grouping tools with outcomes will make it feel more senior.

Suggested edit
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led wording, e.g.: “Analytics strategy, reporting & optimization: GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery, KPI frameworks, executive reporting, SEO/performance analysis.”
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Executive dashboards” for sharper, more standard phrasing.
- If space allows, add one outcome-oriented phrase tied to recent work: “measurement frameworks and dashboards that improved decision-making across web and campaign channels.”
- Keep only the most relevant analytics tools here; order by strategic weight: KPI frameworks, GA4, BigQuery, Power BI/Looker Studio, Clarity, SEO/performance analysis.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This item overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies and the NACo Director bullet on analytics infrastructure; avoid repeating the exact same wording.
- “Power BI” and “Looker Studio” are already substantiated in recent experience, so no need to over-explain them here.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

- “Hybrid and virtual event production” and “Livestreaming” are close; combine if space is tight.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” Since recent roles are strongly Drupal-centered, this item should either sharpen to platform depth/relevance or be trimmed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show level of use: **Drupal (enterprise CMS, migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to be more specific: **CMS Platforms** or **Web CMS Platforms**
- If you want more impact, replace weaker/older tools with stronger current context only if accurate, e.g. keep focus on platforms used in recent NACo work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**, which already lists the same CMS tools.
- “Web & CMS administration” also appears in Core Competencies, so avoid repeating the exact same framing three times.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this item reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Make it feel more current and implementation-focused, emphasizing tools you actively use in recent roles.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: Technical Implementation: HTML/CSS/JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
- Drop version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the CV uses versioning consistently elsewhere; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner.
- Consider grouping by function for readability: Front-end: HTML/CSS/JavaScript, jQuery • Integrations: APIs, GTM • Deployment/automation: Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions
- If space allows elsewhere, tie 1–2 tools to outcomes in recent roles rather than listing only here (e.g., front-end implementation in Drupal, deployment automation, tag management/analytics support).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates Topline Skills [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery,” “API integrations”); keep one section broader and this one strictly tool-based.
- “Workflow automation” appears in Topline Skills; avoid repeating automation language here unless you specify the actual tools only.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow architecture strength. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already called out in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize capability, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems.”
- Tighten to the most relevant tools: “Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams”; drop older/lower-signal items unless actively used.
- If format allows, add light grouping for clarity: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project management: Jira, Asana | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- Best option: add a short impact cue instead of a pure list, e.g. “Built editorial planning, intake, and cross-team coordination workflows using Airtable, Power Automate, Jira, Asana, Slack, and Teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills; avoid repeating both sections with identical wording.
- Basecamp and Trello may feel dated relative to recent senior-level work unless they were materially used in the last few roles.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant tools, but this line is too bare compared with the rest of the CV and misses the candidate’s stronger positioning in email operations and audience engagement. It should signal scale or function, not just list platforms.

Suggested edit
- Rename to: Email Marketing & Engagement Platforms
- Tighten and standardize: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
- If accurate, add functional context instead of more tools: enterprise email campaigns, newsletter operations, audience segmentation, journey automation
- Best upgrade if space allows: Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp | Newsletter operations, segmentation, and automated engagement campaigns

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating “email newsletters reaching tens of thousands” here; that impact is already stronger in recent NACo experience.
- Don’t add generic “digital communications” language; it duplicates Core Competencies and Work Experience.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and, if possible, quantify outputs to show early impact without repeating leadership claims covered in 2018–2024 entries.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize foundational build work: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve production workflows across web, email, social and video.”
- Add concrete scope/results where possible: website refresh size/timeline, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience growth, email/social performance, or production volume.
- Tighten the closing clause to show light supervision, not full management: “mentored a digital media associate on daily production and publishing.”
- Possible version: “Promoted across two digital roles to help launch NACo’s first in-house digital team, streamline multi-channel production workflows, support a major website refresh, and produce recurring livestream and weekly video content.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “strengthening workflows” and “weekly video updates” overlap with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on team formation and hands-on production.
- Avoid repeating broad channel ownership already established in the Director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo roles in digital/multimedia. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo program and policy teams; helped translate findings into digital and multimedia content.”
- Make the second sentence more outcome-oriented: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or output: number of projects supported, episodes produced, audiences reached, or teams/stakeholders served.
- Keep this item shorter than later NACo roles so the progression toward digital leadership remains clear.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid broad phrases like “digital content production and multimedia materials,” which are covered more strongly in 2015–2024 roles.
- Don’t overstate ongoing digital leadership here; save web/video operations language for the later manager/director entries.
